From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Reynolds <alex@finlytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Redwood SDK quickstart & auth/routing follow-up

Hi Alex - thanks for the questions. High-level answers + quick snippets to get you going. I also attached a tiny sample app (sample-app.zip) that includes Python and TS quickstarts.

1) Embeddings -> vector DB
- Quickstart includes a script to compute embeddings and push to RedisVector/Pinecone. You can swap the client implementation; see the utils/embedding_push.py in the sample app. For PoC, running locally against a managed Pinecone instance works fine.

Python example (embedding + upsert):
```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_API_KEY}")
emb = client.embeddings.create(model="rw-embed-1", input="Customer support KB article text")
# push emb['vector'] to your vector DB (Pinecone/Redis)
```

TypeScript example (query + rerank):
```
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
const emb = await client.embeddings.create({ model: 'rw-embed-1', input: text })
// use your vector DB to retrieve top-K ids, then call Redwood.rerank() on the candidate list
```

2) Reranker hosting / routing
- You can host rerankers as a separate model endpoint, or use Redwood routing policies to keep reranker and encoder on same capacity tier for low-latency. For initial PoC we recommend separate endpoints to iterate quickly; switch to co-located routing once latency profiling justifies it.

3) Structured output & tool calling
- SDK supports schema-constrained responses via the `structured` response type and model affordances (function/tool calling). For strict JSON, provide an OpenAPI-like schema to the call and the SDK will attempt to validate/return structured output. We also surface the raw model output for additional validation server-side. Example: `client.chat.create({structured: {type: 'json', schema: {...}}})`

4) Auth (API keys vs OIDC)
- For hosted/Dedicated: API keys are simplest for PoC.
- For Private (VPC/on-prem): we support OIDC + Okta; we handle token exchange and JIT mapping into RBAC. I'll loop in our SE who owns SSO for a short setup call if you go that route.

Suggested agenda for the integration call (30-60 min):
- 10 min: confirm architecture & goals (latency/cost targets)
- 20 min: walkthrough of sample app + quickstart (Python + TS)
- 20 min: discuss auth & network (Okta OIDC, private endpoints, IP allowlists)
- 10 min: next steps (P0 blockers, timeline)

Links: sample repo -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-quickstart

If you want, I can paste a short runnable docker-compose snippet from the sample-app that runs the quickstart locally using an emulator for the vector DB.

--
